games.title: Herzog
games.note: Technosoft's real-time war game for Japanese home computers; its sequel was Herzog Zwei.

games.title: AirMech
games.note: A free-to-play game built as a spiritual successor to Herzog Zwei, with a transforming robot that carries units.

games.title: Future Cop: LAPD
games.note: Its Precinct Assault mode, a duel of bases and spawning units, is sometimes called the first MOBA-style game.

games.title: Demigod
games.note: Wikipedia calls it the first stand-alone commercial game in the MOBA genre.

games.title: Empire Earth
games.note: Rick Goodman, a lead designer of Age of Empires, founded the studio; it spans history from the Stone Age to the future.

games.title: Risk
games.note: Created by French filmmaker Albert Lamorisse as La Conquête du Monde.

games.title: Monopoly
games.dev: Parker Brothers (from Lizzie Magie's The Landlord's Game)
games.note: Descends from Lizzie Magie's 1904 The Landlord's Game; Parker Brothers published Monopoly in 1935.

games.title: Ogre Battle: The March of the Black Queen
games.note: Yasumi Matsuno's strategy RPG, which Wikipedia says blurred the line between tactics RPG and real-time strategy.

games.title: Powermonger
games.note: Bullfrog's follow-up to Populous: you lead a warlord's army across a living map instead of wielding divine powers.

games.title: Godus
games.note: Peter Molyneux's Kickstarted return to the god game; the PC version never left early access.

games.title: Flight Simulator (subLOGIC)
games.note: Bruce Artwick's flight simulator for the Apple II, dated 1979 or early 1980; Microsoft licensed it for the IBM PC.

games.title: Shapez 2
games.note: The 3D sequel, released in early access, adds exploration, layers and mass transport of shapes.

games.title: Command & Conquer: Red Alert 2
games.note: A Soviet invasion of America with mind control, chronospheres and campy live-action briefings.

games.title: Daisenryaku
games.note: SystemSoft's long-running series of hex-based modern war games for Japanese computers.

games.title: Fire Emblem Awakening
games.note: Made as possibly the last Fire Emblem if it sold poorly; its success revived the series worldwide.

links.took: Technosoft's real-time battles of bases and units.
links.added: A transforming jet you fly yourself, split-screen two-player battles and a console release.

links.took: A transforming mech that flies units around and fights alongside them.
links.added: Free-to-play online matches with lanes, unlockable units and co-op.
links.extra: Wikipedia says Herzog Zwei's influence appears in AirMech.

links.took: A two-sided battle where each player is one powerful unit amid spawning forces.
links.added: A shooter's mech, outposts to capture and a computer or human opponent.
links.extra: Wikipedia says the Precinct Assault mode resembles Herzog Zwei.

links.took: The hero-based lane battle that DotA popularized.
links.added: A boxed commercial release with giant demigods, some of them walking siege towers.

links.took: Gas Powered Games' studio and large-scale battle tech.
links.added: A move from army strategy to commanding a single hero.

links.took: Age of Empires' historical RTS and advancement through ages, from one of its lead designers.
links.added: Fourteen epochs from prehistory to a robot future, and air and space units.
links.extra: Wikipedia says Empire Earth refined Age of Empires' historical focus and age advancement.

links.took: Conquering a world map split into territories against rival powers.
links.added: Cities, science, diplomacy and thousands of years of history.
links.extra: Sid Meier has named Risk as his favorite childhood board game.

links.took: World conquest as a game of armies across a map.
links.added: A hidden map to explore and cities that produce armies, ships and planes.
links.extra: Walter Bright named Risk, Stratego and the film Battle of Britain.

links.took: A board-game model that encourages players to interact, trade and compete around one table.
links.added: A planet to settle, real-time auctions and robot mules that farm and mine.
links.extra: Wikipedia says Monopoly was used as a model because it encourages social interaction.

links.took: Yasumi Matsuno's Ogre world, units and alignment system.
links.added: Turn-based battles on isometric maps with height, and a branching war story.

links.took: Lane defense with plants against zombies.
links.added: Time-travel worlds, plant food boosts and free-to-play on phones.

links.took: The Tycoon-style park sim that RollerCoaster Tycoon popularized.
links.added: Animals with their own habitat needs, and guests who come to see them.

links.took: Building and running a zoo, the genre Zoo Tycoon popularized.
links.added: Detailed animal welfare, genetics and breeding, and free-form 3D building.

links.took: Frontier's 3D park-building engine and free-form construction tools.
links.added: Hundreds of simulated animals with welfare, genetics and habitats.

links.took: Bullfrog's living, isometric map full of small people.
links.added: Commanding an army of followers, with seasons, food supply and conquest.
links.extra: Same studio and lead designer, Peter Molyneux.

links.took: Sculpting land so followers can settle and grow, with powers tied to belief.
links.added: Layered terrain to carve and a phone-friendly, free-to-play structure.
links.extra: Wikipedia says Godus was heavily influenced by the Populous series; both are Molyneux games.

links.took: Digging a dungeon, attracting monsters and fighting off heroes.
links.added: Full 3D graphics, more rooms and a My Pet Dungeon sandbox mode.

links.took: Bruce Artwick's flight model and 3D graphics engine.
links.added: A version for the IBM PC published by Microsoft, starting the long-running series.

links.took: Asobo's whole-planet simulator built from map data.
links.added: Career missions such as firefighting, search and rescue and cargo flights.

links.took: SCS Software's trucking simulation and company management.
links.added: The western United States, with states released one by one.

links.took: Abstract factory building with shapes to cut, rotate, paint and stack.
links.added: 3D graphics, exploration, layers and mass transport.

src.t: tobspr, shapez source code readme, GitHub

links.took: The alternate-history war between the Allies and the Soviets.
links.added: A Soviet invasion of America, garrisonable buildings and stranger weapons.

links.took: Turn-based modern warfare between armies of tanks, aircraft and infantry.
links.added: A simpler, friendlier war game for younger players on the Famicom, on a square grid.
links.extra: The goal was reportedly a game like Daisenryaku for a younger audience.

links.took: Total Annihilation's huge armies, commanders and flowing economy.
links.added: Wars on round planets across a solar system.
links.extra: Pitched as a spiritual successor by Total Annihilation veterans.

links.took: Listed by Factorio's developers as an inspiration.
links.added: A factory that builds itself through automation, defended against aliens.

src.t: Factorio wiki (Wube), What is the game inspired by?

links.extra: The source does not say which part of the Civilization series.

links.took: Listed by Factorio's developers as an inspiration.
links.added: Automation instead of colonist stories.

src.t: Factorio wiki (Wube), What is the game inspired by?

links.extra: The source does not say which part; RimWorld was in public alpha from 2013, during Factorio's development.

links.took: Warcraft III's heroes, such as Arthas, Illidan and Thrall.
links.added: A hero brawler mixing them with characters from other Blizzard games.

links.took: Tank artillery duels with hundreds of weapons.
links.added: Online multiplayer, leveling up and unlockable weapons.
links.extra: Listed among the variants Scorched Earth inspired.

links.took: Bullfrog's isometric worlds of busy little people, led by Peter Molyneux.
links.added: A theme park to build and price, with rides, shops, staff and fussy visitors.
links.extra: Same studio; Molyneux co-designed Theme Park with a teenage Demis Hassabis.

links.took: Julian Gollop's turn-based squad combat, first tried on the ZX Spectrum.
links.added: Alien invasion, base building, research and a global war layer.
links.extra: Wikipedia calls Rebelstar and Laser Squad precursors to X-COM by the same developer.

links.took: Grid tactics with characters who can die permanently.
links.added: An optional casual mode, pairing units in battle and children of married characters.

links.took: Relationship building between battles and optional casual mode.
links.added: A school setting, teaching students, and three branching routes.
